content.key_idea: An agentic LLM's think-act-observe loop repeatedly dispatches tool calls across a region boundary to remote knowledge sources, and measured on Search-R1/H100 this remote data retrieval consumes 40-50% of total execution time.

summary: Figure 1 motivates Cortex by illustrating the agentic LLM workflow and its cost. Panel (a) shows Users interacting with an Agentic LLM that runs an iterative think-act loop, dispatching tool-call actions over MCP to remote Search Engine, Private RAG, and Data Lake services that typically sit in a different region. Panel (b) walks through a concrete Search-R1 example, showing the think/search/info/answer tag sequence used to look up who painted the Mona Lisa from Remote Data. Panel (c) is a stacked bar chart breaking down per-step latency of Search-R1 on an H100 GPU into Inference (orange) versus Data Retrieval (blue) time across reasoning steps, showing retrieval consumes roughly 40-50% of total execution time. Together the three panels establish that remote data access is a first-class latency and cost bottleneck for agentic LLM serving.
